old_caption: The video captures a scientific experiment setup involving a long, transparent glass tube mounted horizontally on a metal stand. The tube is secured at both ends with orange plastic caps, each containing a white substance. A white, cloudy substance is present in the middle section of the tube and is visibly moving and diffusing. The background consists of a plain blackboard, suggesting an educational or laboratory setting. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the tube and its contents, providing a clear view of the dynamic condition of the substance.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a scientific experiment setup involving a long, transparent glass tube mounted horizontally on a metal stand. The tube is secured at both ends with orange plastic caps, each containing a white substance that appears to be a solid or semi-solid material. The middle section of the tube is filled with a clear liquid, possibly water, which is being manipulated by a thin, flexible tube inserted from one end. As the video progresses, the liquid inside the tube begins to bubble and foam, indicating a chemical reaction or gas production. The background consists of a plain blackboard, suggesting an educational or laboratory setting. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the tube and its contents, providing a clear view of the ongoing process without any noticeable changes in angle or movement.
caption: The video captures a horizontal clear glass tube held at its midpoint by a metal clamp on a vertical stand, with blue plastic stoppers near the clamp and orange end caps containing white cotton plugs at both openings. A faint white vapor occupies the right half of the tube, spreading slowly leftward toward the central clamp while remaining separated from the left cotton plug. At the right opening, a slender transparent rod, angled into the tube near the cotton plug, is gradually pulled outward to the right. As it moves, the rod rotates toward a more horizontal orientation and its tip moves out of the tube, then the rod disappears from view. The white cloud continues to creep leftward and becomes slightly more diffuse, but it never reaches the left end of the tube. The stand, clamp, stoppers, plugs, caps, table caps, and blackboard remain fixed, with no camera movement.
